title: The Stones Across the Stream

title: The Seed Finds Down

before.title: The Seed Finds Down
before.text: A bean seed grew in a dark jar. No sun showed it which way to grow. Still, its first root went down. Its green stem went up. A child turned the jar on its side. That pull helped the root find water below and helped the stem rise toward light.

after.title: The Seed Finds Down
after.text: A bean seed started to grow in a dark jar. Its first root went down. A pale shoot went up. A child turned the jar on its side. After some time, the root bent down again. The shoot bent up. The new plant had no eyes. It could respond to the pull of the earth, even in the dark. Later, the shoot could reach light above the soil.

reason: Indiana University’s plant observation confirms roots can respond to gravity in darkness while shoots orient upward. “Green stem” without light and “root finds water below” imply too much; describe a pale shoot and gravity response separately from later access to light.

title: The Echo by the Wall

before.text: Mia stood in a wide yard near a high wall. She clapped once and heard the same sound come back. No one was on the far side. Mia took ten steps away from the wall and clapped again. after.title: The Echo by the Wall

reason: An echo is reflected sound, but ten steps near a wall may not give a distinct change in delay. Place Mia far enough from the wall, then farther away, and name the longer round trip.
